events.name: screen_viewed

payload.name: screen_id
payload.type: str — canonical snake_case key from enums.json §11. Stable forever; never re-used, never edited.

payload.name: screen_name
payload.type: str — the human label from enums.json §11, verbatim. What you search for in the analytics tool. May be edited when the screen is renamed.

payload.name: last_used
payload.type: str — OPTIONAL, SCREEN-SCOPED. Which auth method the user last signed in with. Only meaningful on a screen that offers a method list (signup_welcome_back, signup_create_account, connect_sso). OMIT everywhere else — it has no value on a profile step, and an empty string is worse than an absent property (decision 29).

payload.name: state
payload.type: str — OPTIONAL, SCREEN-SCOPED. For a screen whose registry row covers many states (§11 rule: one row per screen, not per state), this says which one. Only connect_sso uses it, and it is KNOWN BROKEN there — always "idle", because screen_viewed fires once on mount and the state changes afterwards. OMIT on every other screen. It cannot describe the DoB or verify-email states, which are carried by their own events (decision 29).

events.required_payload: screen_id, screen_name, referrer_screen_id — these three, on every screen, always. last_used and state are optional and screen-scoped; see each one. A flat payload list is not a statement that every property applies everywhere (decision 29).
events.trigger: Screen view controller finishes rendering. Every screen in the registry fires this event; the screen is a property rather than part of the event name, which is what lets one funnel span screens.
events.code_delta: Keep screen_name exactly as it ships — no rename (decision 27). ADD screen_id alongside it, taken from the enums.json §11 registry, and referrer_screen_id. Both come from the registry row, not from a literal at the call site.

events.required_payload: step_id and time_on_step_s, always. prompt_count only on step_id: "prompts" — and required there (v1.4.1).

events.name: profile_step_skipped

payload.name: step_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §2; the Media screen has two: media_video and media_voice

payload.name: has_video
payload.type: bool — OPTIONAL, SCREEN-SCOPED. Media screen only: what the profile already held when the step was skipped.

payload.name: has_voice
payload.type: bool — OPTIONAL, SCREEN-SCOPED. Media screen only.

events.trigger: Optional step bypassed via the "Skip" CTA. On the Media screen, Skip sits beside an always-enabled Continue and the step carries two ids (media_video, media_voice) for one screen, so step_id says which card the skip is recorded against and screen_id says where it happened.
events.required_payload: step_id and screen_id, always. "Skip" exists on several optional steps and a skip with no screen reference cannot be funnelled — added in v1.4. has_video / has_voice only on profile_media.

events.name: photo_slot_tapped
events.trigger: Photo slot tapped, or the “Add more” control revealing optional slots 5–6 (action: "reveal_optional")

events.name: photo_added
events.trigger: Image selected and set in slot

events.name: photos_minimum_met
events.trigger: Minimum required photos (4 of 6) uploaded — fires once, on the first crossing

events.name: prompt_topic_list_opened
events.trigger: The “Browse all 15 topics” control tapped, opening the topic sheet. Read against screen views of the step, this is how often the three suggestions were not enough.

events.name: prompt_topic_list_dismissed
events.trigger: The topic sheet closed WITHOUT a topic being picked — the X, the scrim, a swipe-down or the system back gesture. Picking a topic replaces the sheet with the write sheet and fires prompt_topic_selected instead, so this event and that one are mutually exclusive and together they close the browse sheet's funnel: opened (prompt_topic_list_opened) → picked or cancelled. Added 16 Sep 2026: the write sheet had an abandonment event and the browse sheet did not, so a user who opened all fifteen topics and closed the sheet was invisible. Read against prompt_topic_list_opened, a high rate means the fifteen are not the problem the suggestion cards were solving.

events.name: prompt_topic_selected

payload.name: selection_index
payload.type: int — 1-based count of topic selections in this visit to the step. 1 is the topic the user reached for FIRST, which is not the same question as which topic they saved.

events.trigger: A topic chosen — a suggestion card on the screen or a row in the browse sheet. The two are deliberately NOT distinguished: entry_point and position were removed on 25 Sep 2026 (taxonomy 1.4.4), because the question is which topics are chosen, not where. DOES NOT FIRE ON EDIT from v1.4.1: reopening a saved prompt is not a fresh choice of topic; prompt_editor_opened{is_edit:true} covers that. THE event that answers which topics people choose, and with selection_index, which one they tried first. topic_id from enums §17.

events.name: prompt_editor_opened
events.trigger: The write sheet mounted — on a suggestion card, on a row of the browse sheet, or on the pencil pip of a saved prompt. THIS IS THE EDIT EVENT: is_edit: true is the pencil being tapped, and from v1.4.1 it is the only event an edit fires at open (prompt_topic_selected no longer does). Paired with prompt_saved / prompt_editor_dismissed, this is the per-topic completion rate: how many people open a topic and how many finish it.

events.name: prompt_example_dismissed
events.trigger: The worked example hidden with its X. Low volume by design; if it is high, the example is in the way rather than helping.

events.name: prompt_char_limit_reached
events.trigger: The answer first reached 160 characters in this editor session. Fires once per session, not per keystroke. Says whether the cap is the right number — it is currently unvalidated.

events.name: prompt_saved
events.trigger: Save pressed with a non-empty answer. NEVER send the answer text — length_bucket only (enums §19). prompt_count is the number of prompts the user holds after this save.

events.name: prompt_editor_dismissed

payload.name: dismiss_method
payload.type: "close"|"backdrop"|"swipe"|"system_back" — enums.json §23. Was close|scrim|swipe|back until v1.4.1; migrated to the one canonical sheet vocabulary.

events.trigger: The write sheet closed without saving. THE abandonment event this screen is designed against: a user who opened a topic, typed something and left is the drop-off that was previously invisible. had_draft is what separates “changed their mind” from “could not finish”. is_edit (added 25 Sep 2026, replacing entry_point: "edit") separates backing out of an edit from abandoning a new prompt.

events.name: prompt_deleted
events.trigger: A saved prompt removed. Not reachable from the profile-creation screen (there is no delete there) — it exists for profile editing, and is registered here so that flow cannot invent a second name.

events.name: prompts_minimum_met
events.trigger: The first prompt was saved, so the step can be completed — fires once, on the first crossing. The prompts sibling of photos_minimum_met, and the single number that says whether this screen works.

events.name: media_screen_viewed

payload.name: preview_video_prompt_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §20; the prompt previewed on the empty video card at this view

events.trigger: The Media screen ("Show your face") finishes rendering. has_video / has_voice carry the entry state of BOTH slots, which is what makes every later retake or delete on this screen attributable to a user who already had an artefact — the question the two booleans exist to answer. Fires on every mount, including the return from an accepted recording, so the state change is visible as two consecutive views. Was type: "voice"|"video" until v1.4: one screen carries both cards, so the screen view is not per medium — the medium belongs on the acts below. The two preview ids record which prompt each empty card displayed, because from v1.4 that is server-ranked rather than fixed (decision 33) — without them the ranking cannot be evaluated against the behaviour it produced.
events.required_payload: screen_id, has_video, has_voice, and both preview_*_prompt_id + preview_source — every mount. WHAT WAS SHOWN IS NOT DERIVABLE AFTER THE FACT: the ranking changes, so a view that does not record the two prompts it displayed cannot be attributed later.

events.name: media_prompt_list_opened
events.trigger: "See the prompts" tapped, opening the prompt list for one medium. Replaces media_inspiration_opened (v1.4): the "Show me what works" inspiration sheet was removed from the kit on 16 Sep 2026 and the eleven-prompt list took its place, so topic_id no longer applies — the chosen prompt is carried by media_prompt_selected instead. has_existing separates opening the list with an empty card from reopening it over something already recorded.
events.required_payload: type is REQUIRED. One screen carries the video card and the voice card, and an event without type cannot be attributed to either.

events.name: media_prompt_selected

payload.name: was_previewed
payload.type: bool — true if this prompt was the one shown on the empty card at the time the list was opened

events.trigger: The commit CTA ("Film 10 seconds" / "Record 15 seconds") tapped with a row selected — the prompt the user actually took into the camera, not every row they tried on the way. STORE AND SEND THE ID, NEVER THE DISPLAY STRING (§20): the prompts are copy and will be edited. type scopes it, because the same eleven are offered for both media and "which prompt gets chosen" is a different answer for video than for voice. selections_before counts the rows tapped and abandoned first — a list that takes four taps to settle is a list that is too long. was_previewed is the feedback-loop guard: the previewed prompt is more visible than the other ten, so the ranking that feeds the preview is computed with those selections EXCLUDED (decision 33). An event without it makes the ranking self-reinforcing and unmeasurable.

events.name: media_prompt_list_dismissed

payload.name: dismiss_method
payload.type: "close"|"backdrop"|"swipe"|"system_back" — enums.json §23. cancel was renamed close in v1.4.1 so every sheet in the product shares one value set.

events.trigger: The prompt list closed without going to the camera — the X, the backdrop, a swipe-down, or the system back gesture. had_selection: true is a user who picked a prompt and then backed out, which is a different signal from one who read the list and left; both are the drop-off the list is accountable for. Uses dismiss_method, not method — see §8 on the two vocabularies that collided under method.

events.name: video_recording_started
events.trigger: Video capture actually begins on the recording screen — permission already granted, timer running. Was prompt_id: str until v1.4; renamed media_prompt_id because prompt_id is already the written-prompt key (§6, §17) and the two registries are unrelated. attempt counts takes of the same prompt, starting at 1, so a retake loop is readable without diffing timestamps.

events.name: video_prompt_recorded
events.trigger: "Use this clip" accepted on the review screen — NOT on Stop. Stopping produces a take; accepting produces the artefact, and only this event means the profile gained something. A take that is stopped and then retaken never fires it. The user returns to the Media screen, where the next media_screen_viewed carries has_video: true.

events.name: voice_recording_started
events.trigger: Voice capture actually begins on the recording screen — permission already granted, timer running. Was prompt_id: str until v1.4; renamed media_prompt_id because prompt_id is already the written-prompt key (§6, §17) and the two registries are unrelated. attempt counts takes of the same prompt, starting at 1, so a retake loop is readable without diffing timestamps.

events.name: voice_prompt_recorded
events.trigger: "Use this recording" accepted on the review screen — NOT on Stop. Stopping produces a take; accepting produces the artefact, and only this event means the profile gained something. A take that is stopped and then retaken never fires it. The user returns to the Media screen, where the next media_screen_viewed carries has_voice: true.

events.name: media_review_shown
events.trigger: Stop tapped, or the length cap reached, and the review screen mounts — play / retake / keep. The denominator for everything that follows a take: media_preview_played, media_retaken{from:"review"} and video_prompt_recorded / voice_prompt_recorded are all choices made on this screen, and none of them is interpretable without knowing how many takes reached it. stop_reason separates a user who finished early from one who ran out of seconds.

events.name: media_preview_played
events.trigger: Play tapped on the review screen. Fires per play with a running count, starting at 1 — whether people watch or listen back before keeping a take is the question the review screen exists to answer, and a single event with no count cannot tell a confident keep from a nervous one.

events.name: media_prompt_ranking_published

payload.name: media_prompt_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §20; the prompt now previewed for this medium

events.trigger: The ranking job publishes the preview prompt for one medium — once per medium per refresh, and ONLY when the published value changes. The audit trail for decision 33: a preview that moved has to be attributable to a sample and a window, or a drop in recording rate cannot be told apart from a bad prompt. Server-side; the client never ranks and never computes a preview locally.

events.name: media_retaken
events.trigger: Retake tapped — either on the review screen, discarding the take just made, or on a filled card on the Media screen, replacing something already saved to the profile. had_video / had_voice carry what the profile held at that moment, so a retake by a user who already has both media is distinguishable from a first-time loop.
events.required_payload: type and from are both REQUIRED. from is what separates a discarded draft from a replaced artefact; without it the two collapse into one number that means neither.

events.name: media_deleted
events.trigger: Delete tapped on a filled card on the Media screen — the artefact is removed from the profile and the card returns to empty. Deleting is not retaking: there is no replacement take, and collapsing the two would read a user giving up as a user trying again. had_video / had_voice are the state BEFORE the deletion.

payload.name: field_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §1 field_id. Interests (Profile 21) fires one per answered "How I live" group: activity · diet · alcohol · smoking · rhythm · social (v1.4.7)

payload.name: value_bucketed
payload.type: str — the enums.json §1 value. Multi-select dating_language: the ticked §1 values in list order, comma-joined, no spaces (v1.4.12)

events.name: field_display_opted_out
events.trigger: “Don't show on my profile” switched on was: opt-out checkbox ticked — opt-out only, no event on untick. Absence for a field_id = displayed, so this answers which fields people hide but never how many hide it right now — that reads off the hidden_fields user property (Properties §P3). Eight controls: the seven Share some details screens with a ProfileVisibility band (height → politics) and age on the DoB step v1.2. Interests (Profile 21) has no switch — fully public, decided 8 Oct 2026; habits was cut

payload.type: int — "What I'm into" picks after this tap, 0–10. "How I live" chips never count

payload.name: tag_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §3 (registry 1.4.16), never the chip label

events.name: show_more_expanded
events.trigger: Any “Show more” control expanded in place. section_id from the tag_id section slugs on Interests; screen_id is what tells you where it happened. Photos keeps photo_slot_tapped action:"reveal_optional" rather than duplicating this

events.trigger: Tap on a faded chip while 10 "What I'm into" interests are picked — the tap is a no-op. Fires on every such tap. "How I live" is uncapped and never fires this

events.trigger: Future screen (Profile 23): accepted Continue with at least one pick — one event per answered question, in list order (family_ahead → partnership_ahead → living_ahead). An unanswered question sends nothing. Never per tap

events.trigger: SUPERSEDED 16 Sep 2026 — DO NOT FIRE. Written prompts are instrumented in family E only, against enums §17 / §19.

This is the v1.0 name for editing an existing prompt; the live event is prompt_editor_opened{is_edit:true} → prompt_saved{is_edit:true} in family E, with the payload the Profile 07 ticket specifies. The row is kept, emptied of its payload, so that the name resolves to this notice instead of being re-implemented from a stale spec. Written prompts are instrumented in family E only, against enums §17 / §19.

events.name: permission_prompted
events.trigger: Our own pre-permission surface shown, before any OS sheet — a modal OR a full screen. From 25 Sep 2026 the notifications case is Stay reachable (Profile 10, profile_reachability): fires on view with type: "notifications" when the OS status is not_determined. Profile 09 NO LONGER fires it — 09 raises no sheet any more. Location (from 5 Oct 2026): Profile 12 (profile_location) fires it on view of the ask state with type: "location" — never on the denied or services_off states. The location gate does NOT fire it — its pre-permission event is location_gate_shown with reason not_determined (22 Oct 2026).

events.name: permission_os_sheet_shown

payload.name: screen_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §11. OPTIONAL: sent by the location gate as search_location_gate. Absent on Profile 12 (built 5 Oct 2026 without it) — absent means profile_location. Added 22 Oct 2026 (Search 04).

events.trigger: System permission dialog triggers. Notifications: raised by Save preferences on Stay reachable (Profile 10), only when the push toggle is on and the status is not_determined — moved from Profile 09 on 25 Sep 2026. Location: raised by 'Allow location access' on Profile 12, type: "location". Location gate (Search 04, 22 Oct 2026): raised by 'Allow location access' in state A, with screen_id: "search_location_gate".

events.name: permission_result

payload.name: screen_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §11. OPTIONAL: sent by the location gate as search_location_gate. Absent on Profile 12 (built 5 Oct 2026 without it) — absent means profile_location. Added 22 Oct 2026 (Search 04).

events.trigger: User responds to OS permission dialog. Location: precise and approximate are both granted, and so is iOS Allow Once / Android Only this time; limited never applies. Location gate: carries screen_id: "search_location_gate".

events.name: permission_denied_recovery_shown

payload.name: reason
payload.type: str — enums.json §26 location_unavailable_reason: denied | services_off. REQUIRED when type is location, absent otherwise. Added 5 Oct 2026.

events.trigger: Recovery banner shown after denial. Location: Profile 12's denied and services_off states, with reason. NOT fired by the location gate — location_gate_shown with reason denied / services_off is that surface's event (22 Oct 2026).

events.name: permission_settings_opened

payload.name: screen_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §11. OPTIONAL: sent by the location gate as search_location_gate. Absent on Profile 12 (built 5 Oct 2026 without it) — absent means profile_location. Added 22 Oct 2026 (Search 04).

events.trigger: Deep-link to OS App Settings tapped. Location: Profile 12 B/C and the location gate B/C (gate sends screen_id: "search_location_gate").

events.name: permission_status_changed

payload.name: from
payload.type: str — enums.json §24 permission_status; the last value the client synced

payload.name: to
payload.type: str — enums.json §24 permission_status; the value just read

payload.name: in_flow
payload.type: bool — true when the change is detected while the user is still inside profile creation

events.required_payload: type, from, to and detected_on always. from is what the SERVER was last told, not what the screen last saw — a change the client never synced is exactly the case this event exists for.
events.trigger: The OS permission status read on launch or foreground differs from the last value the client synced: the user changed it outside our app (Settings, an OS update, a Focus mode, Android's per-channel switches) or a restore carried a different one in. NOT the answer to our own dialog — that is permission_result, and the two must never both fire for one act. Emitted by the shared permission reconciler, not by a screen.

events.name: consent_changed
events.trigger: A consent toggle changed, in either direction — on:false is the opt-out, on:true the opt-in. TWO PLACES FIRE THIS. (1) The marketing checkbox on the profile Email screen: channel:"marketing_email", surface:"profile_creation". The address itself is not a consent — it is used for password resets and support replies regardless; the checkbox governs marketing mail alone, so an unchecked box means no marketing, not no email (decision 28). (2) The six Stay reachable toggles: channel is one of the other six values. surface is required on both — a consent record that cannot be traced to where it was given cannot be honoured. MVP (25 Sep 2026): Stay reachable fires this for channel:"push" ONLY. An interest checkbox is not a consent and fires channel_interest_changed instead — never consent_changed.

events.name: channel_interest_changed
events.trigger: An interest checkbox on Stay reachable (Profile 10) checked or unchecked — every flip, in order. The MVP demand test for channels that do not exist yet. NOT a consent: never fire consent_changed for it, never collect contact data for it, never send on it. The final state is reachability_saved.interest. NEW 25 Sep 2026.

events.name: reachability_saved

payload.name: push_on
payload.type: bool — the push consent the user leaves with

payload.name: permission
payload.type: str — enums.json §24, read after the OS sheet (or on arrival if none was raised)

payload.name: interest
payload.type: [str] — enums.json §25; the boxes checked at Save, [] if none

events.trigger: “Save preferences” tapped and the save confirmed by the server — the state the user actually leaves the screen in, which per-toggle events cannot reconstruct. THE DENOMINATOR-SIDE ROW OF THE DEMAND TEST: share of screen_viewed{profile_reachability} whose reachability_saved.interest contains a channel. Payload changed 25 Sep 2026 for the MVP scope: channels_on, count and has_phone removed (no phone field, one consent channel). Stay reachable has no skip, so profile_step_skipped does not fire here.

events.name: check_in_started
events.trigger: User taps “Check-in for a date” on the Check-In intro (checkin_intro). Not fired when the gate reopens at Today — that path (intro passed before) skips the intro.

events.name: check_in_closed

payload.name: step_id
payload.type: enums §28 check_in_step — the screen the ✕ was tapped on

events.trigger: User taps the ✕ on any Check-In screen and lands on checkin_search_unavailable. Availability (today, tomorrow) and the uplift text are DISCARDED; motivation, vibe and filters keep their last accepted answer. Check-In 01 emits step_id intro; each step ticket adds its own value. Uplift (06): step_id uplift; ✕ is inert while a commit is in flight.

events.name: check_in_gate_tapped

payload.name: intro_passed
payload.type: bool — the user has tapped the intro CTA at least once; decides the destination: true → today step (empty), false → checkin_intro

events.trigger: On checkin_search_unavailable (date search not available), the user taps the CTA, the Search tab or the Instant tab — all three reopen the Check-In. Settings does not fire it.

events.name: check_in_step_answered

payload.name: step_id
payload.type: enums §28 check_in_step (today · tomorrow · motivation · vibe · filters · uplift)

events.trigger: User taps Continue on a Check-In step and it is accepted (never on the intro). On today / tomorrow (Check-In 02) answer_value is "hours" when ≥ 1 hour is picked and "none" for an empty Today confirmed with continue_tomorrow — the hour detail is availability_slots_set. time_to_answer_ms runs from that step's screen_viewed. Fires again on every accepted Continue, including a pre-filled draft Continued unchanged. On motivation (Check-In 03) answer_value is "prefilled" (the pre-selected last answer Continued unchanged) or "picked" (first Check-In, or changed); the value itself is motivation_selected (Class 1). On vibe (Check-In 04) answer_value is "prefilled" (the pre-selected set Continued unchanged) or "picked" (first Check-In, or the set changed); the values are vibe_selected. On filters (Check-In 05) answer_value is "prefilled" (the shown settings Continued unchanged) or "picked" (anything changed); the settings are check_in_filters_changed. On uplift (Check-In 06) answer_value is "written" (non-empty after trim) or "empty"; it fires ONCE, when the commit SUCCEEDS — not on the tap, so a failed save and a retry fire it once. The text itself is never sent.

Never per chip tap; never on the max-reached toast; never on ✕. Respecified 13 Oct 2026 (Check-In 04, taxonomy 1.4.14): was payload value, trigger “Vibe tag selected for upcoming window”.

payload.name: items

events.name: like_withdrawn

payload.name: match_id
payload.type: str | null — the match that caused the withdrawal; null when reason is no_overlap

events.trigger: One per open like that closed without a decision: matched = either person's other like became mutual first (1 match = 1 date); no_overlap = the two Check-Ins have no meet-time overlap left (Search 03). NEW 1.4.17 (Search 01); reason NEW 1.4.19.

events.name: like_expired
events.trigger: A sent like closes without an answer. Negative label for the like-back estimate (matching phase 1+). Not fired for like_withdrawn or a declined like (pass_sent covers that).

events.name: pass_sent
events.trigger: Not now or Not interested on the full profile (surface profile), or Not interested on a Likes received card (surface likes_received). not_now = hidden until the next Check-In; not_interested = removed from the pool for good, and on a received like also declines it (the liker is not told). Fires on the tap, EXCEPT for a declined received like: on Likes received (the card, or a Liked-you profile opened from it; surface likes_received) and on a Liked-you profile opened from the grid (surface profile) it fires when the 6 s Undo window ends or the user leaves the screen; an Undo fires pass_undone and no pass_sent. reason_if_given REMOVED 20 Oct 2026. A grid card has no pass buttons.

events.name: likes_received_viewed

payload.name: open_count
payload.type: int — open likes on the list; the same number as the Likes tab badge. RENAMED from count 1.4.19

payload.name: closed_count
payload.type: int — closed cards on the list (Too late + Out of time), not yet seen on a previous visit. NEW 1.4.19

events.trigger: Likes tab list loaded (Search 03), once per visit to the tab. Fires with 0 / 0 on the empty state. Returning from a profile does not fire it again. is_locked REMOVED 1.4.19: the screen is Premium-only.

events.name: pass_undone

payload.name: position
payload.type: int — the card's 1-based position on the list

events.trigger: Undo tapped on the decline toast within its 6 s window: on Likes received (surface likes_received, Search 03) or on the grid after Not interested on a Liked-you profile (surface profile, Search 02). The card returns to its previous state and nothing was sent. NEW 1.4.19.

events.name: like_confirm_failed
events.trigger: Confirm date in Be sure (mutual) refused by the server because the like closed first. The first confirm to reach the server wins. Back on the Likes list, or on the grid for a profile opened from it (Search 02), the card is closed in place: matched → Too late, no_overlap → Out of time. surface is profile on both: the confirm is only ever made on the profile. NEW 1.4.19 (Search 03).

events.name: search_coach_shown
events.trigger: The actions coach ("Three ways to decide") is drawn over the first profile of a Search visit: the first queue profile (Freemium, Search 01) or the first profile opened from the grid (Premium, Search 02). Shown on every visit until the user taps Don't show again; at most once per visit. Not on the Likes tab or a Liked-you profile (their third button is Confirm date). An empty queue shows no coach and fires nothing. NEW 1.4.20; amended 21 Oct 2026 before hand-over (was once per account).

events.name: search_coach_dismissed

payload.name: dismiss_method
payload.type: str — enums.json §23 sheet dismiss_method: close = Got it or Don't show again · backdrop = scrim tap · system_back = Android back. swipe is never sent (the coach has no drag).

payload.name: dont_show_again
payload.type: bool — true only for the Don't show again button; then the server stores the per-user flag and the coach never shows again. Scrim and Android back are always false.

payload.name: visible_ms
payload.type: int — ms from search_coach_shown to the dismissal

events.trigger: The actions coach is closed. Got it, a scrim tap and Android back close it for this visit only; Don't show again also sets the per-user flag (server). Backgrounding or killing the app while it shows fires nothing. NEW 1.4.20; dont_show_again added 21 Oct 2026 before hand-over.

events.name: location_gate_shown

payload.name: reason
payload.type: str — enums.json §26 location_unavailable_reason (not_determined · denied · services_off). Was inline undetermined|denied|device_off until 5 Oct 2026.

events.trigger: The location gate (Search 04, screen_id search_location_gate) is shown: once on mount with the current §26 reason, and again only when the reason changes while it is mounted (e.g. the phone's Location turned on but the app still denied: services_off → denied). Not on every foreground. Never fired by Profile 12. Respecified 22 Oct 2026; was "Location required blocker displayed".

events.name: search_empty_shown
events.trigger: The Search no-results state becomes visible, once per visit, with reason no_results; not for loading or a failed request. Returning from Filters begins a new visit. Approved 27 Oct 2026 (Search 01, taxonomy 1.4.24).

reconciled_with_code: Reconciled against both apps' shipped code, 12 October 2026: 94 events implemented -- 86 client events that production code on BOTH Android and iOS actually fires (definitions alone, tests and the debug developer menu do not count), and 8 server events the backend emits. Supersedes the 7 September 2026 catalogue (35 events). Names for the built flows follow the code; unbuilt events keep their spec names. 13 Oct 2026: merged into handoff registry 1.4.25 / taxonomy 1.4.16 (Check-In 01-06); the reconciliation above was carried over event by event, and event_count is the real count (the handoff file said one fewer). 19 Oct 2026: 11 more turned on, the 48hrs Check-In's ten client events and permission_status_changed (the shared permission reconciler), each fired by production code on both apps: 105 implemented, 97 client and 8 server. 19 Oct 2026, later: signup_code_verify_failed fires again (on a code the server refused, with its 1-based attempt), so it is implemented and its code_delta is gone: 106 implemented, 98 client.
screen_identity_note: Two properties, on purpose. screen_id is the stable machine key and never changes. screen_name is the human label and is what a person searches for in the analytics tool. Only screen_viewed carries both; every other event carries screen_id alone and joins to it. Both values come from the enums.json §11 registry — never typed at a call site.
